The given label is "No conflict" because all non-irrelevant documents refer to the same concept—South Sea pearls being found in the South Sea/South Pacific region—and are in agreement. Differences are only in the granularity of listing specific countries or coasts within that region (d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d9).

The evidence uniformly points to the South Sea (or South Pacific) as the sea where the pearls in question are found. Documents d1, d4, d8, and d9 explicitly state the name originates from the shell's location in the "South Sea" or southern hemisphere. Others specify countries and coasts within that broad region, which are complementary details rather than contradictions.

FINAL ANSWER
South Sea pearls are found in the South Sea, a region in the southern hemisphere [d4, d9]. More specifically, they are cultivated in waters off northern Australia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Myanmar, and Thailand [d1, d3]. The pearls come from the Pinctada maxima oyster, which inhabits this South Pacific area [d3, d9].
